A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the four ripening groups were distinguishable late in ripening by OPLS, this distinction is not based on metabolite variation alone.

, late in ripening in Pinot Noir, the most significant differences between ripening classes of fruit were found in seed and skin metabolite profiles and that, in these two tissues, the most significant changes in metabolites occurred between pairs of time points rather than across all time points.

, while the berries within a cluster are not identical at véraison, the variation in metabolites is dynamic over time, and the differences in metabolites between berries at a given time point may be as important as those between time points.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developmental position of fruit at véraison is an important determinant of berry ripening and composition late in ripening.
there is significant developmental inequality late in ripening and that this is associated with variation in metabolites.
the metabolic profiles of berries are not uniform late in ripening.
